questions.q: What method must a class implement to satisfy the Queueable interface?
questions.explain: The Queueable interface requires exactly one method: execute, which takes a QueueableContext parameter.

questions.q: Why can a Queueable job's constructor accept a List<Account> directly, when a future method cannot accept an Account parameter at all?
options: A Queueable instance is serialized as a whole object, so it can carry sObjects and other non-primitive types, unlike a future method's primitive-only parameters
Account is secretly a primitive type in Apex
Queueable Apex doesn't actually support sObject parameters either — this is a common misconception
Future methods can accept Account too, as long as it's wrapped in a List
questions.explain: Because a Queueable instance is serialized whole, it can carry real sObjects and custom Apex classes directly in its constructor — one of Queueable Apex's clear advantages over the primitive-only restriction on future methods.

questions.q: What does System.enqueueJob return, and what does that enable that a future method call doesn't?
options: It returns the Id of the new AsyncApexJob record, letting you track and query the job's status later
It returns a Boolean indicating success or failure immediately
It returns nothing at all, exactly like a future method
It returns the full serialized Queueable object
questions.explain: System.enqueueJob returns the Id of the newly created AsyncApexJob record, which you can store and query to check Status, NumberOfErrors, and other job progress fields — something a future method call gives you no way to do.

questions.q: What is required, in addition to implementing Queueable, for a job's execute method to make an HTTP callout?
options: The class must also implement Database.AllowsCallouts
Nothing extra is required — Queueable jobs can always make callouts
The method must be annotated with @future(callout=true)
The class must extend the built-in HttpCallout base class
questions.explain: A Queueable class that performs callouts must also implement Database.AllowsCallouts; without it, attempting a callout inside execute throws a runtime error.

questions.q: How many times can a single transaction call System.enqueueJob, assuming that transaction is itself running synchronously?
options: There is no limit at all
questions.explain: A synchronous transaction can call System.enqueueJob up to 50 times. If the calling code is itself already running asynchronously, it's limited to enqueuing just one job.
